name: Melville Syrah Estate Donna's Block 2018
text:
## Melville Syrah Estate Donna's Block 2018

**The story.** Melville is a family-owned estate founded in 1989 by Ron Melville, who grew sought-after grapes in Sonoma County's Knights Valley. In 1996 his wish to grow cold-climate Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Syrah brought the family to the [Sta. Rita Hills](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Melville+Winery,+Lompoc,+California,+USA&t=k) in the western [Santa Ynez Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Ynez_Valley) of [Santa Barbara County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Barbara_County,_California); today Ron and his son Chad run what Melville calls one of California's most highly regarded estates ([Melville](https://melvillewinery.com/estate/history/)). The family was heavily involved in creating the [Sta. Rita Hills AVA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sta._Rita_Hills_AVA), granted in 2001 ([Melville](https://melvillewinery.com/estate/vineyards/)).

**The vineyards.** Melville farms 120 acres in the heart of the Sta. Rita Hills, mostly on Lompoc dune sand with clay loam and shallow hardpans of Monterey shale, planted densely at 1,812 vines per acre, with 8 clones of Syrah among others. Every block is fermented in small lots and kept separate through ageing. The ocean is only ten miles away: morning and evening fog and steady afternoon winds lengthen the season and keep natural acidity, which is why Melville can make Syrah in a cool place better known for Pinot Noir ([Melville](https://melvillewinery.com/estate/vineyards/)). Melville's philosophy: "At the time of harvest, we consider the wines to already be made and strive not to interfere with their natural path" ([Melville](https://melvillewinery.com/estate/history/)).

**The wine: Donna's Block.** Donna's Block is one of Melville's small-lot estate [Syrahs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah), from a single block of its Sta. Rita Hills vineyards, which are fermented and aged separately ([Melville](https://melvillewinery.com/estate/vineyards/)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [northern California vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/northern-california) says early rain gave the vines a healthy start in 2018, then a cool autumn allowed prolonged ripening and slightly larger yields than 2017; "throughout the state and across varieties", generally good-quality wines with good ageing potential.

**What the critics say for 2018.**
- I couldn't read the critics' notes for the 2018 Donna's Block (retailers cite high scores from Jeb Dunnuck, Wine Enthusiast and Wine & Spirits, but the pages I could open didn't show them), so I've left scores out rather than guess.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.7** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is eight years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2022 to 2034. So it is in its drinking window, with plenty of time. Decant an hour ahead and serve at 15 to 17°C, slightly cool to show off the perfume.

**Food.** Cool-climate Syrah suits grilled lamb with herbs, duck, Santa Maria-style tri-tip (a Santa Barbara County barbecue tradition), or pork with black pepper.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Melville at the moment.

**Curious details**
- **Dune sand.** Much of the estate is planted on ancient Lompoc dune sand ([Melville](https://melvillewinery.com/estate/vineyards/)).
- **Founders of an appellation.** The Melvilles helped create the Sta. Rita Hills AVA in 2001 ([Melville](https://melvillewinery.com/estate/vineyards/)).
